text: The ABS/DSC hydraulic unit reports a fault with its electric pump motor.
hint: Check the DSC unit's ground and power first; common cause is worn pump motor brushes or a failing motor, often fixed by rebuilding or replacing the hydraulic unit.
notes: Sources list E90/E91 (actronics) and E90-E93 plus E8x (ecu-fix); often appears together with 5DF1.

text: The ABS/DSC hydraulic unit reports a problem at the pump motor's electrical connection.
hint: Common cause is a poor contact or corroded/burnt connector between pump motor and DSC control board; check the unit's ground strap before buying parts.
notes: Usually logged alongside 5DF0.

text: The pressure sensor built into the ABS/DSC hydraulic unit has failed or gives an implausible reading.
hint: The sensor is internal to the hydraulic unit, so the usual fix is repairing or replacing the DSC unit; rule out low battery voltage first.
notes: Reported on E87 and E90/E91; one of the most common E8x/E9x DSC failures.

text: DSC has detected a problem in its communication or torque-control interface with the engine computer.
hint: Often a follow-on of an engine fault that puts the car in limp mode; read and fix the DME codes first.
notes: Meaning taken from thread titles on E8x (babybmw) and E9x M3 (m3post) forums.

text: The steering angle sensor needs to be calibrated (zero-point / serial number adjustment) to the DSC.
hint: Run the steering angle sensor adjustment with wheels straight and steering wheel level; needed after SZL, DSC or alignment work.

text: DSC finds the steering angle sensor signal implausible compared with other vehicle data.
hint: In a documented E90 case the cause was a damaged code disc inside the steering column switch cluster (SZL), not the DSC.

text: DSC logged an internal fault reported by the steering angle sensor.
hint: The steering angle sensor sits in the steering column switch cluster (SZL); inspect the SZL before replacing the DSC.
notes: The source says this was stored in the DSC on an E90, together with 5EBA and 94B5.

text: DSC logged an internal fault of the steering column switch cluster (SZL).
hint: Common cause in the documented case was a damaged steering angle code disc in the SZL.

text: DSC reports a fault with the front-left wheel speed sensor signal.
hint: Check the sensor connector and wiring at the front-left hub, then the sensor itself.
notes: Wheel position confirmed by a MINI (same DSC family) thread and a sensor supplier's code list; E90 thread confirms the code occurs on E9x.

text: DSC reports an implausible direction-of-rotation signal from the front-left wheel speed sensor.
hint: Common cause is a failing or wrong-type wheel speed sensor at the front left.

text: DSC reports a fault with the front-right wheel speed sensor.
hint: Inspect the front-right sensor, its wiring and connector.

text: DSC reports a fault with the front-right wheel speed sensor signal.
hint: Inspect the front-right sensor, its wiring and connector.

text: DSC reports a fault with the front-right wheel speed sensor.
hint: Common cause is a failing front-right wheel speed sensor.

text: DSC reports a fault with the rear-left wheel speed sensor.
hint: Inspect the rear-left sensor, wiring and connector.

text: DSC reports a fault with the rear-left wheel speed sensor signal.
hint: Inspect the rear-left sensor, wiring and connector.
notes: Chassis evidence is an E87 118i video; same DSC family as E9x.

text: DSC reports a fault with the rear-left wheel speed sensor signal.
hint: On an E91 335i the cause was a worn rear wheel bearing (the sensor reads the bearing's encoder ring).

text: DSC reports a fault with the rear-left wheel speed sensor.
hint: Inspect the rear-left sensor, wiring and connector.

text: DSC reports a fault with the rear-left wheel speed sensor.
hint: Inspect the rear-left sensor, wiring and connector.

text: DSC reports an electrical fault in the power supply of the rear-right wheel speed sensor.
hint: Check the rear-right sensor wiring for shorts or chafing and measure supply voltage at the connector before replacing the sensor.

text: DSC finds the rear-right wheel speed sensor signal implausible.
hint: Inspect the rear-right sensor, its encoder ring and wiring.

text: DSC reports a fault with the rear-right wheel speed sensor.
hint: Inspect the rear-right sensor, wiring and connector.
notes: Chassis for this exact code not confirmed beyond BMW DSC family; wheel position from sensor supplier list.

text: DSC reports an implausible direction-of-rotation signal from the rear-right wheel speed sensor.
hint: Common cause is a failing or incorrect rear-right wheel speed sensor.

text: Brake pad wear warning from the front-axle pad wear sensor.
hint: Check front pad thickness; the wear sensor must be replaced with the pads and the service interval reset.
notes: bmwtuning (E90 guide) lists 5F12-5F16 as DSC brake pad sensor codes; front-axle detail from youcanic.

text: DSC finds the rear-axle brake pad wear sensor signal implausible.
hint: Check rear pad thickness and the rear wear sensor wiring; replace the sensor with new pads.

text: The gearbox computer saw the wrong gear ratio during the 5th-to-4th downshift.
hint: Common causes are old or low transmission fluid, mechatronic sleeve leaks or worn clutches; check fluid level and condition first.
notes: Reported by an E90 325 owner in the sayyarti comments.

text: The gearbox computer saw the wrong gear ratio during the 4th-to-5th upshift.
hint: Check transmission fluid level and condition; may indicate clutch wear.
notes: Chassis evidence is an E87 118d (same ZF 6HP family as E9x).

text: The gearbox computer detected an incorrect gear ratio involving internal clutch E (slip).
hint: Can be clutch wear or low hydraulic pressure; check fluid level and condition before condemning the gearbox.
notes: Sources describe ZF 6HP19/21/26 generally (6HP19 is the E9x gearbox) but do not name E9x for this code.

text: The gearbox computer saw the wrong gear ratio during the 6th-to-5th downshift.
hint: Identifies a failed shift event, not necessarily a dead gearbox; check fluid and adaptations.
notes: Source covers ZF 6HP19/21/26 generally.

text: The gearbox computer detected an incorrect gear ratio involving internal clutch D (slip).
hint: Check fluid level and condition; persistent clutch slip codes may point to worn clutch packs.
notes: Meaning from one source; E9x threads confirm the code occurs on E90/E92.

text: The gearbox computer detected an incorrect gear ratio involving internal clutch A (slip).
hint: Check fluid level and condition; persistent clutch slip codes may point to worn clutch packs.
notes: Meaning from one source; E90 thread confirms the code occurs on E9x.

text: Intermittent gearbox faults and emergency mode caused by an incorrectly fitted mechatronic connector sleeve.
hint: BMW service bulletin SI B 24 08 06 covers this on ZF 6HP gearboxes; inspect or replace the sleeve and refill fluid.
notes: Source cites the bulletin as covering E90-E93 among others; listed together with 507A.

text: Intermittent gearbox faults and emergency mode caused by an incorrectly fitted mechatronic connector sleeve.
hint: See BMW SI B 24 08 06; inspect or replace the sleeve and refill fluid.
notes: Listed together with 5079 for E90-E93.

text: Airbag module reports a fault in the driver's seat belt pretensioner igniter circuit.
hint: Common cause is a loose or damaged connector at the pretensioner (often after seat or trim work).
notes: Two video titles (one naming E90) agree on driver pretensioner, but a generic blog (ancel.com) gives a different meaning, so marked medium.

text: Airbag module reports a fault with the passenger seat occupancy detection.
hint: In a documented E90 case the occupancy sensor was unplugged and its cable torn; check its connector, power, ground and LIN line.
notes: A repair-shop site (airbag24) gives a different meaning; the E90-specific case is used here.

text: Airbag module reports a fault with the passenger seat occupancy sensor.
hint: Check the seat occupancy mat/sensor wiring under the passenger seat.
notes: Both are E90 threads tying the code to the occupancy sensor; neither gives the exact sub-fault.
